name: Spellcraft Learning Progression
status: current stress-tested learning progression with explicit beginner/intermediate/advanced boundaries
purpose: The current Cuspell-first teaching path. Checkpoint 141 stress-tests the full 29-sign progression and separates the 11-sign first-lesson core, an 18-sign beginner course, a 24-sign intermediate composition course, and a 29-sign advanced extension. The old 50-sign v0.1 file remains a coverage benchmark rather than a learning target.
design_rules: teach one reusable semantic pattern at a time
prefer explicit objective references This/You/There
teach Begin/End state transitions before acquisition, attributes, or creation
introduce Find only in its simple yes/no form
teach attribute-setting before fresh creation so Create can reuse an already-known Change pattern
introduce exactly one typed fresh binder in the creation module
teach an objectively designated TimeInterval reference before maintenance/prevention
teach Persist before Prevent so duration is learned on a StateProposition before nesting an EventSpec
teach only Prevent's simple exact-EventSpec form here; bound EventSpec interception remains advanced
keep the semantic core free of duration/protection, representation, multi-target programming, and time-flow machinery
teach representation on an existing carrier before multi-channel or composite illusion programming
teach Vision as the first explicit SenseChannel without requiring Sense
treat Represent as a persistent carrier/content/channel state, not as forced perception or truth
reuse prior Begin/End/Persist/Create patterns instead of adding And or Sign to this module
teach And first only as proposition/state conjunction; event-level And transaction semantics remain advanced
teach Sequence and Concurrent together so ordered and simultaneous event composition are contrasted explicitly
teach finite Repeat only after ordinary event composition and reuse the already-known quantity notation
teach multi-target magic only through an explicitly bounded/resolvable collection; singular Process frames never distribute silently
teach simple Trigger only after ThisInterval is already known; bound-witness Trigger remains advanced
include Sequence in programming teaching because Create continuation is special-purpose and does not replace general ordered execution
teach TimeFlow first with an explicit Entity reference and an already-known positive integer rate
do not require Zero or Divide merely to understand relative time-flow
teach stopped/slower time as optional extensions after the core TimeFlow relation is understood
keep time reversal outside TimeFlow; negative factors remain invalid
syntax_taught_in_core: flat tight local application; parentheses are not required

first_actions.purpose: One movement Process plus a state that can begin or end.

reusable_state_vocabulary.purpose: Add an explicit other target plus two high-yield state words; no new grammar.

bounded_discovery.purpose: Add caster reference and simple factive yes/no Find.

starter_spells.name: Move selected thing
starter_spells.note: Move the designated subject to the designated destination.

starter_spells.name: Move another person
starter_spells.note: Reuse Move with the explicit target You.

starter_spells.name: Mark magical
starter_spells.note: Begin the Entity's Magic state; this does not by itself add a hidden magical behavior.

starter_spells.name: Dispel selected magic state
starter_spells.note: End the selected Entity's Magic state/effect marker.

starter_spells.name: Check integrity
starter_spells.note: Acquire the truthful yes/no answer about Whole.

starter_spells.name: Check whether it is locked
starter_spells.note: Acquire the truthful yes/no answer about Locked.

starter_spells.name: Detect magic
starter_spells.note: Acquire the truthful yes/no answer about the Entity's Magic state.

modules.name: Attribute change and Light

spells.name: Make an existing thing luminous
spells.note: Set the Light output of an already-existing designated Entity.

modules.rationale: Change has a three-part attribute-setting pattern and Light introduces a measured quantity, so it is taught after the 11-sign core instead of arriving together with Create.

modules.name: Fresh creation
syntax_additions: Create profile followed by one immediate continuation EventSpec

spells.name: Create light at the designated destination
spells.note: Allocate one fresh spatial Entity at There, then immediately set that same fresh Entity's Light output.

modules.rationale: Creation genuinely needs binder scope and a profile/continuation distinction. It therefore reuses the already-known Light/Change pattern instead of teaching all of those ideas in one step.

modules.name: Duration and active maintenance
context_requirements: ThisInterval must resolve to one objectively designated TimeInterval supplied by the command/casting environment
ThisInterval is not a duration literal and does not mean forever

spells.name: Maintain integrity
spells.note: Actively maintain the selected Entity's Whole state against ordinary evolution for the designated interval. Persist is not taught as a synonym for Begin.

spells.name: Keep locked
spells.note: Actively maintain the Locked state over the designated interval.

spells.name: Maintain magical state
spells.note: Actively maintain the Entity's Magic state over the designated interval.

modules.rationale: This stage adds one temporal reference plus one operator. It reuses StatePropositions already learned in the 11-sign core and introduces finite active maintenance without event matching.

modules.name: Exact-event protection

spells.name: Prevent movement to the destination
spells.note: Block the exact Move(This, There) EventSpec over the designated interval.

spells.name: Protect against being broken by this state transition
spells.note: Block the exact End Whole This EventSpec over the designated interval; this does not automatically describe every physical way Whole might cease.

spells.name: Prevent locking
spells.note: Block the exact Begin Locked This EventSpec over the designated interval.

modules.teaching_scope: Only Prevent(event, interval) is taught here. The bound matcher form with :«ThisEvent»:MoveSelfHere, predicates, optional Region scope, and generic antimagic interception is deferred to advanced spell programming.
modules.rationale: Prevent adds one semantic sign but one new structural idea: an EventSpec is passed as the thing to block. Teaching it after Persist means the learner already understands the interval argument.

modules.name: Shared visual representation
new_concepts: SenseChannel as an explicit representation channel
carrier and represented content are distinct
representation is shared/objective state; observers are not enumerated
represented content need not be true or physically present

spells.name: Begin visual depiction
spells.note: Make the designated carrier This begin visually depicting You.

spells.name: End visual depiction
spells.note: End that visual representation state.

spells.name: Maintain visual depiction
spells.cuspell: Persist Represent This You Vision ThisInterval!
spells.note: Actively maintain an already-established visual representation over the designated interval.

spells.name: Create a fresh visual representation carrier
spells.cuspell: Create :«This» At $«This» There Begin Represent $«This» This Vision!
spells.note: Create a fresh Entity at the designated destination, then make it begin visually representing This. Exact visible realization still depends on deterministic world/media rules.

modules.teaching_scope: Only one channel, Vision, is taught. Represent is not Sense: it does not force any observer to perceive, believe, understand, or accept the represented content. It also does not make the represented content physically present or true.
modules.rationale: Two new semantic signs are enough. The learner already knows Begin/End, Persist + ThisInterval, and Create + At + binders. Reusing those patterns avoids prematurely adding And, Sign, Sense, Hearing, TouchChannel, or Trigger.

modules.name: State/proposition conjunction
syntax_additions: same-operator chains remain flat; mixed And/Or grouping is later material

spells.name: Check two facts together
spells.cuspell: Find Self This Whole This And Magic This!
spells.note: Ask one bounded yes/no Find query whose proposition requires both Whole and Magic.

spells.name: Create with a two-fact profile
spells.cuspell: Create :«This» At $«This» There And Magic $«This» Begin Represent $«This» This Vision!
spells.note: Conjoin At and Magic inside the fresh Entity profile, then reuse the immediate continuation to begin its visual representation.

modules.teaching_scope: And is introduced as proposition/state conjunction only. In flat surface syntax, the surrounding typed frame determines where that proposition belongs; the lesson avoids event-level And composites, whose transactional execution semantics remain advanced.
modules.rationale: One semantic sign exposes compositional propositions without yet introducing event-level transactional And. Find and Create both already provide typed Proposition slots, so they demonstrate conjunction cleanly without parentheses.

modules.name: Ordered and concurrent event composition
syntax_additions: Sequence and Concurrent consume flat EventSpec lists
sentence end closes the final list; standalone colon closer are only needed when later same-sentence material follows

spells.name: Move then mark magical
spells.cuspell: Sequence Move This There Begin Magic This!
spells.note: Execute Move first; only after it succeeds, evaluate/execute Begin Magic against the resulting world state.

spells.name: Move one target while marking another magical
spells.cuspell: Concurrent Move This There Begin Magic You!
spells.note: Request the two component EventSpecs concurrently rather than in order.

modules.teaching_scope: Sequence means ordered execution with no free rollback of earlier successful steps. Concurrent means component events occur concurrently. Neither is replaced by Create's one special profile/continuation scope.
modules.rationale: The prior candidate list included Concurrent but accidentally omitted Sequence. General programming needs both ordered and simultaneous composition, so they are taught as a contrastive pair.

modules.name: Finite repetition

spells.name: Create three fresh lights
spells.cuspell: Repeat @@@ Create :«This» At $«This» There Change $«This» Light «LightUnit» @!
spells.note: Repeat the entire fresh-creation EventSpec three times. Each Create invocation allocates a distinct identity.

modules.teaching_scope: Only finite count-based Repeat is taught. The count must be a nonnegative integer Quantity. No unbounded loop or implicit forever behavior exists.
modules.rationale: Repeat adds one compression operator and reuses quantity notation already introduced by the Light module plus an EventSpec already understood from Create.

modules.name: Simple reactive programming

spells.name: Auto-unlock watcher
spells.cuspell: Trigger Locked This End Locked This ThisInterval!
spells.note: During the designated lifetime, watch for the Locked proposition and attempt End Locked This when the trigger transition occurs.

spells.name: Auto-dispel selected Magic state
spells.cuspell: Trigger Magic This End Magic This ThisInterval!
spells.note: Watch the selected Entity's Magic state and attempt to end it when the trigger condition fires.

modules.teaching_scope: Only Trigger(condition, action, lifetime) is taught. It is one-shot by default and requires a finite explicit lifetime. The bound-witness Trigger form that exports a matched binder into its action remains advanced.
modules.rationale: Trigger reuses known Propositions, EventSpecs, and ThisInterval. Delaying it until after those pieces are familiar avoids teaching watcher lifetime, condition, action, and binder export simultaneously.

modules.name: Bounded multi-target distribution
syntax_additions: Collect introduces a typed selection binder
Each introduces a second binder for one member of the resolved collection
context_requirements: This must designate an Entity whose group membership is objectively resolvable/finite enough for the active execution context
Collect does not grant omniscient world search
Each distributes only over the explicitly resolved collection

spells.name: Mark every member of a designated group magical
spells.cuspell: Each Collect :«This»:This Member $«This» This :«You»:This Begin Magic $«You»!
spells.note: Collect the Entity members of designated group This, bind each member as y, and instantiate Begin Magic for every resolved member.

spells.name: Illuminate every member of a designated group
spells.cuspell: Each Collect :«This»:This Member $«This» This :«You»:This Change $«You» Light «LightUnit» @!
spells.note: Reuse the same bounded collection/distribution pattern with the earlier Light attribute operation.

modules.teaching_scope: No singular Process silently applies to a Collection. Collect constructs an explicitly typed collection from resolvable membership; Each performs the distribution. Ordering between member events is not implied.
modules.rationale: Collect, Member, and Each are taught together because none of the three alone gives a useful beginner multi-target command. The explicit group relation supplies the bounded selection context instead of hidden area/world search.

modules.name: Relative local time-flow

spells.name: Accelerate another entity relative to the caster
spells.note: Maintain the target's local physical/process temporal progression at factor 2 relative to Self over the designated interval.

spells.name: Accelerate the caster relative to another entity
spells.note: Maintain Self at factor 2 relative to the explicit reference You. The reference is never silently omitted.

modules.teaching_scope: Only Entity TimeFlow with a positive integer factor is required here. @ means equal progression and @@ means factor 2, reusing number notation already learned earlier. TimeFlow changes the subject's whole local physical/process temporal progression relative to the explicit reference; it is not Repeat, event Rate, movement speed, action-count metadata, or time travel.
modules.rationale: The relation itself is only one new semantic sign because Self/You, @ notation, Persist, and ThisInterval are already known. Stopped time requires the separate Zero quantity sign and slower fractional flow requires arithmetic such as Divide; those are useful optional expansions but not prerequisites for learning TimeFlow.

optional_vocabulary.purpose: Convenience Location reference for caster-local effects; not required because There already supplies a designated Location.
Example of ordinary state-vocabulary expansion after Begin/End/Find are learned.
Second representation channel after Vision is understood.
examples: Persist Represent This You Hearing ThisInterval!

optional_vocabulary.purpose: Tactile representation channel. It does not automatically imply physical Matter, mass, collision, or damage.
Useful carrier classification for inscriptions/images/records, but not required to learn Represent itself.
Zero-mana grammatical closers used only when a flat Sequence/Concurrent must end before later material in the same sentence. Sentence end closes the beginner examples automatically.
Exact stopped local progression for TimeFlow and other zero-valued quantities.
optional_vocabulary.example: Persist TimeFlow You Self Zero ThisInterval!

optional_vocabulary.purpose: Arithmetic extension for fractional TimeFlow factors such as half-speed.
optional_vocabulary.example: Persist TimeFlow You Self Divide @ @@ ThisInterval!

deferred_modules.name: advanced time-flow applications
deferred_modules.note: The required path teaches only positive Entity-relative TimeFlow. Stop-time, fractional slow-time, Region time-flow, nested/boundary cases, and any future time-reversal semantics remain optional/advanced.

deferred_modules.name: advanced programming and bound watchers
deferred_modules.note: Checkpoint 139 teaches state/proposition And and simple Trigger. Event-level transactional And, mixed logical grouping, bound-witness Trigger, conditionals, and branch-selection policy remain advanced.

deferred_modules.name: advanced collection selection
deferred_modules.note: Checkpoint 139 teaches only Collect + Member + Each for an explicitly resolvable group. General selectors, ranking, random selection, and collection analytics remain later material.

deferred_modules.name: multi-channel and programmed illusion
deferred_modules.note: After checkpoint 139, And and simple Trigger are known, but richer carrier profiles, extra channels, bound watchers, and programmed motion remain optional/advanced illusion material.

deferred_modules.name: advanced protection and magical interception
deferred_modules.note: The simple exact-event Prevent form is taught in checkpoint 137. Bound :«ThisEvent»:MoveSelfHere predicate/Region interception remains advanced.

beginner.label: Beginner spellcraft
beginner.rationale: These stages teach direct effect construction, measured change, fresh creation, finite maintenance, and exact-event protection. They introduce binders and EventSpecs but not general control flow, collections, long-lived reactive programming, or altered temporal frames.

intermediate.label: Intermediate composition
intermediate.rationale: These stages add carrier/content/channel representation plus general proposition/event composition and finite recurrence. They are composition-heavy but still avoid nested collection binders, persistent watchers, and temporal-frame manipulation.

advanced.label: Advanced spell programming
advanced.rationale: These stages require persistent reactive watcher semantics, nested selection/distribution binders, or explicit relative temporal progression. Trigger comes before collection distribution because it reuses already-known condition/action/lifetime structures and adds no new binder syntax.

stress_test_findings: Every required example uses only core signs plus semantic signs introduced no later than its own module; no hidden registered-sign prerequisite was found.

The first genuine course boundary appears after exact prevention: shared representation introduces a new carrier/content/channel ontology, and the following stages become general composition/programming rather than direct spell construction.

The old advanced ordering put nested Collect/Each binders before simple Trigger. The stress test reverses those two: Trigger adds one watcher concept but no new binder syntax, while multi-target distribution requires two binder roles plus collection resolution.
Nested collection selection/distribution and relative temporal frames remain qualitatively heavier even when they add few semantic signs.
Therefore 29 signs is a complete staged learning path, not a single beginner vocabulary target.
